body.statement: The published Choi--Yuan model writes \(M^0=M^\star+M^R\), permits nonzero approximation error, imposes global singular-vector incoherence and conditioning, and assumes i.i.d. centered homoskedastic sub-Gaussian noise.  Its staggered-adoption Theorem 3.2 concerns one scalar group-at-time functional and lists six hypotheses: signal, spectral size, missing-block size, approximation bias, global Gram balance, and target-loading nondegeneracy.

source.locator: Section 2, Assumption [Noise], and Theorem 3.2(i)--(vi) in the published author manuscript
